method.label: Use a double root to bound the sum

annotationRationale: The composition splits into two quadratic equations whose distinct real roots are counted with discriminants. Completing the square then bounds the root sum and identifies its unique maximizer.
sourceMethod: Follows the official zero-discriminant argument and quadratic bound on the root sum. Uses r=-t^2 to simplify notation and explicitly checks distinct roots, equality, and feasibility.

review.mathCheck: Three distinct composition zeros force one of the disjoint equations p(x)=r,s to have discriminant zero. Writing r=-t² gives s=-t²±2t and r+s≤1/2, with equality uniquely at r=-1/4, s=3/4. The resulting composition zeros are -3/4, 1/4, 5/4, and p(1)=5/16, choice A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Q25, page 13: the same zero-discriminant condition and quadratic bound. It explicitly supplies the repeated-root exclusion, equality conditions and attainment check.
review.annotationCheck: Statement, choices and key match the supplied source. Distinct-root counts, the domain t>0 and uniqueness are handled explicitly; the explanation is reconstructible at AMC 12 level.
